chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mouse and the dog that fall into the butter and the oil, then come out from it alive, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with eating it.'
ai.seo_question: Is butter or oil still halal if a mouse or dog falls into it and comes out alive?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the principle of *istishab al-hal* (presumption of continuity of purity) in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that the mere presence of an animal in liquid fat does not automatically render it *najis* (impure), provided the animal emerges alive, thereby distinguishing between physical contamination and ritual impurity. This ruling is foundational for understanding how Shia scholars apply the concept of 'little water' and liquid mediums in *fiqh al-maytah* (jurisprudence of dead animals).

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Noman, from Saeed Al A’araj who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the mouse and the dog which fall into the butter and the oil, then come out alive from it’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with eating it’.
